<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **95** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **52** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a5b5635e60523ba75abbf736da56bb43d014d09` — the merge of head `bceed47ae05f2c749415a7b55a496b126dc41db0` into base `ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a5b5635e60523ba75abbf736da56bb43d014d09 && git checkout 8a5b5635e60523ba75abbf736da56bb43d014d09
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394 bceed47ae05f2c749415a7b55a496b126dc41db0 && git checkout -B drift-repro ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394 && git merge --no-ff bceed47ae05f2c749415a7b55a496b126dc41db0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ebfa2bfa180124c403fc037fbea7a23738e30394` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review of #32473 · 2026-11-11T22:52Z

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `bceed47ae05f2c749415a7b55a496b126dc41db0`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and changeset). `check-governed-merges --pr 32473`: no governed path. No `packages/spec/src/**` path.

### ① Derived judgments

- New CLI command `os audit verify` and the `audit` topic: a pure addition, and it is read-only (the verifier reads through `SealStorageReader`, which carries `getDriverForObject` only).
- New exports from `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: `verifyAuditLedger`, `AUDIT_ROW_VERDICTS`, `AuditRowVerdict` and `AuditVerifyReport`. The `audit-seal` barrel also exports `checkpointLeafHashesFromRow` and the report types. All are additions; no export was removed or retyped.
- `sys_audit_checkpoint.leaf_hashes`: a new required, read-only column outside the signed body. The sealer writes it beside every checkpoint. The verifier trusts it only when it rebuilds the signed root (`checkpointLeafHashesFromRow`), and refuses it at any other length. Right: the root authenticates the list, so the column adds no trust of its own.
- `trustedSigningKey` (moved from `LocalCheckpointSigner#trustedPublicKey`) now orders by `id` and refuses a row whose fingerprint differs from the asked key id. This is the same trust rule as before (D6), slightly tighter, and the signer delegates to it. Nothing the signer trusted before is refused, except a row whose fingerprint does not equal its own id, which no writer produces.
- Reads page by `id` (`readAll`, `PAGE_SIZE`), so no verdict is truncated at a default limit.

### ② Semver level

The changeset is patch on `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli`. The additive surface would read minor, but `check-changeset-no-major` refuses minor beside `Metadata-protocol: none` (ruling A, #25105), and the dev states this in the body. Accepted.

### ③ Boundary flags

- New required column on an existing system object: the changeset states that no host composes the sealer with a crypto provider yet, so no deployment holds checkpoint rows to backfill. Accepted on that statement. If a host composes the sealer before this lands, the column needs a backfill rule.
- Missing-table handling at head `bceed47a`: each catch names the object it read (#13440 gate), and any other fault throws, which means exit 2.
- Follow-up, should-fix, not blocking this slice: `trustedSigningKey` turns ANY failure to open a key's private half into "untrusted". That includes a transient read fault on `sys_secret`, which the verifier then reports as checkpoints that hold nothing (exit 1, a tamper verdict) instead of exit 2. This is inherited behaviour of the moved signer code, not new in this PR. It is carried into the P2b dispatch: tell a read fault from a key that does not open.
- The S9 sealer error line on stderr and the S7 row-size note are the dev's out-of-scope flags; they are tracked on #31908.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-btu2u9`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CaAUev5V62cLHhQwBi`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Seat record: ACCEPT #32473 · 2026-11-11T22:53Z · head `bceed47ae05f2c749415a7b55a496b126dc41db0`

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：ADR-0154 D9 的 P2a，新增在线校验命令 `os audit verify`。它只读启动，用 `os serve` 同一个加密提供方打开检查点种子和签名密钥（从不新建密钥），读热库和 `archive` 数据源，把每个已封存行判为 unmodified / modified / missing / late / redacted / expired 之一，并打印它信任的密钥指纹。`sys_audit_checkpoint` 新增一列 `leaf_hashes`，本身不签名，只有能重建出已签名的 Merkle 根时才被信任，这样每一行可以单独判定。
- 为什么改：P1 只写检查点，没人核验；没有 verify，封存就证明不了任何东西。
- 风险与回滚：命令只读，不写任何行。main 上没有对象声明 `lifecycle.seal`，宿主也还没把加密提供方交给封存器（S9），所以合入后现网不会产生检查点，verify 会报「没有封存内容」并以 0 退出。回滚即整体 revert。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/verifier.ts`（信任与判定），`signed-body.ts` 的 `checkpointLeafHashesFromRow`，`packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts`（退出码 0/1/2）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal`，预期 7 个文件、138 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的：席位的落地动作被本会话的自动模式分类器拦下（同 #32464），等你在线程里授权，或你直接转 ready 合并。#31908 不关：P2b（离线证明包）在本 PR 合入后从最新 main 另开 PR。

席位意见：ACCEPT。信任只来自能打开私钥的本部署签名密钥（D6），`leaf_hashes` 只在重建签名根时可信，读取按 id 分页不截断。一项 should-fix（读 `sys_secret` 的瞬时故障会被当作「密钥不可信」，退出 1 而非 2）是从签名器搬来的旧行为，记为 P2b 的跟进项，不挡本片。

## 席位核对

1. Shape: draft PR to `main`. `Part of #31908`, with no closing keyword anywhere in the body. 38 files: the CLI command + test, plugin-audit seal/verifier sources + tests, the object's new column, 12 generated translation files for it, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, and a changeset; all within the claim's surface as amended (6795974647). I read the cli.mdx section against `verify.ts`; its verdict table, the trust sentence and the 0/1/2 exit-code list match the command. A patch changeset on both packages (`private: false`).
2. Premise measured: the dev's step 0 (option A, the unsigned `leaf_hashes` column) is the ruled design. On my own read, the verifier reads through `SealStorageReader` only, and `checkpointLeafHashesFromRow` refuses a list of the wrong length and a list that does not rebuild the signed root.
3. Gates on head `bceed47a`: every check-run is `success` or an expected skip (39 success, 15 skipped, 0 other), including Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check and Test Core. `mergeable_state` is `clean`; K = 7. The first head `feddf5e4` was red on the #13440 `isMissingTableError` callers gate. The patch round named the read object at both call sites, with two ablations recorded, and the derived gates for `verifier.ts` re-ran green (49/49).
4. Accepted deviations: changeset graded patch, because `check-changeset-no-major` refuses minor beside `Metadata-protocol: none`; the fault field is `kind`, not `code` (`check:error-code-casing`); exit 2 also covers a crypto refusal, an unconnected archive, and a check that stopped partway (documented). Contract review: TIER_DEFAULT PASS, comment 6809031647, on this head.
5. Out of scope: the S9 sealer error line and the S7 row-size widening (dev flags, tracked on #31908). The should-fix above rides the P2b order. Skills-docs: none (Metadata-protocol: none).
6. Landing: NOT governed, 2532 lines ≤ 3000, Tier S. Held with `pm:awaiting-merge` behind the same auto-mode classifier refusal as #32464 (Merge Without Review); the landing stroke was not attempted again.
